identity.title: $p\textrm{-less}$ Sampling: A Robust Hyperparameter-Free Approach for LLM Decoding

problem.claim: LLM output quality depends on choosing a sampling-based decoding strategy, with settings potentially varying by task and temperature.

gap.claim: Existing sampling methods can be sensitive to hyperparameter choices, limiting robustness across generation conditions.

contributions.claim: Introduces p-less sampling, which dynamically sets a truncation threshold from the full token probability distribution at each decoding step.
Provides theoretical perspectives intended to ground the proposed sampling method.
Evaluates p-less across math, logical reasoning, and creative writing tasks, including efficiency, qualitative, case-study, and diversity analyses.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish p-less from existing methods by proposing a hyperparameter-free sampler whose threshold adapts to the entire token distribution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that p-less consistently outperforms existing sampling approaches and degrades less in text quality as temperature rises.
The authors report lower average token sampling times and shorter generation lengths than alternatives, without sacrificing accuracy.
The authors report empirical validation across math, logical reasoning, and creative writing tasks, supported by qualitative examples, case studies, and diversity assessments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sampling-based decoding affects LLM output quality, but existing methods may require condition-specific hyperparameter settings.
The paper introduces p-less, dynamically deriving a truncation threshold from the full token distribution without hyperparameters.
It presents theoretical perspectives and evaluates the method across mathematical, reasoning, and creative-writing tasks.
The authors report quality, high-temperature robustness, inference-time efficiency, and supporting qualitative and diversity analyses.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a decoding decision to the entire token probability distribution and separately reports quality, temperature robustness, efficiency, and diversity outcomes.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes more informative when its decision rule and multiple evaluation dimensions are explicitly connected.
lessons.application: When presenting an adaptive algorithm, state the observable signal driving adaptation, then align evaluation with quality, robustness, cost, and behavior.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method has no interpretable adaptive signal or when some evaluation dimensions are outside the intended use case.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark datasets, baselines, numerical effect sizes, temperature ranges, or statistical uncertainty.
The reported efficiency and accuracy comparisons lack implementation and evaluation-condition details in the abstract.
